sources.title: House Delivery approved public Concierge pricing statement, version 2026-11-13.2, fact prices
sources.notes: Carries CAD denomination and planning-only scope. Does not establish a model-specific quotation.

facts.text: House Delivery is an Indigenous-owned Canadian housing company combining housing design, manufacturing, procurement, logistics and Canadian construction expertise. Its founder brings more than 35 years of manufacturing and commercial experience.

House Delivery serves developers, municipalities, institutions, non-profits, First Nations and Indigenous communities, alongside individual homeowners and ADU customers. A project may be one home or a repeatable, phased housing program.
Light-gauge steel, domestic timber and other suitable engineered systems can be considered for the project; a model rendering does not fix the final construction specification.

Depending on the project, the housing system may include domestic timber or light-gauge steel manufactured internationally. Qualified Canadian construction professionals undertake site work, foundations, assembly and completion under an agreed scope.
qualifiers: No verified public country-by-component matrix. Do not name a country, factory or partner from private knowledge.

facts.text: The supplied home package is an engineered kit of components and selected materials. Package contents, finishes, freight and applicable import costs are established in the written project quotation.

Site preparation, foundations, service connections, local engineering and permits, Canadian assembly and completion, appliances and sales taxes are separately considered unless expressly included. Delivery access and special logistics also need review; a package price is not a turnkey construction price.

The Salt Spring Design Studio displays Premium at $250 per sq. ft. and Signature at $300 per sq. ft. House Delivery’s approved public pricing statement identifies CAD home-package planning references; these are not completed-home prices or firm quotations.
qualifiers: The observed display is Salt Spring residence-level tier controls. A rate is not a verified price for another model.
Confirm model applicability, chargeable area, selected scope and delivery in a written quotation.

facts.text: Essential is described as a durable coordinated baseline; Premium adds refinement in materials and detail; Signature introduces selective feature finishes. The inclusions page lists Premium and Signature for custom homes, and Essential and Premium for laneway/carriage and pre-reviewed homes.
qualifiers: The inclusions page offers Essential/Premium for compact and catalogue homes; the homepage describes Premium as the catalogue starting point. This is an ambiguity about default versus available tiers, not proof that Essential is unavailable.
Confirm the selected design’s baseline. No current Essential rate is verified.

facts.text: Visible selections can coordinate flooring, tile and surfaces, kitchens, wardrobes, interior doors, exterior openings, bathrooms, lighting and window coverings. Final products and specifications are confirmed for the selected home and project.

Where the model offers Design My Home, its curated room and finish choices create a personalized Look Book. The images establish design intent; actual products, availability, quantities, price and technical suitability need project review.
Model-specific Design Studio choices coordinate finishes. Layout, structural and exterior changes can be discussed through project-specific design and engineering review.
qualifiers: A visual selection does not authorize a structural change or establish a free redesign.

facts.text: Appliances are project coordinated; final package and model selections are confirmed during project review. They must be budgeted separately unless expressly included in the written scope.

Published design boards do not establish final product ratings or code compliance. Site-specific professionals must confirm the selected structure, envelope, services and local authority requirements.

Begin with the site and housing need, choose models and quantities, set design directions, review scope and readiness, then authorize the next project stage. Site-specific professional work and approvals precede the relevant manufacturing and construction commitments.

Factory preparation and site work can progress in parallel where approvals, procurement and site readiness permit. Logistics and the agreed supply package are coordinated with Canadian assembly teams.
House Delivery welcomes discussion with your existing builder. The general contractor remains responsible for local site execution, trades and construction management under the agreed scope.
Timing depends on the agreed design, approvals, site readiness, procurement, delivery and Canadian construction plan.
qualifiers: No universal production, shipping, assembly or move-in duration is verified.

facts.text: The free preliminary property review uses available government property information and can require manual review. It is not a survey, formal zoning determination, engineering assessment or guarantee of approval.

You do not need completed architectural plans to start a conversation: a property, idea or preferred model is enough. The sales team reviews the project and follows up personally; an inquiry creates no purchase commitment.

CMHC catalogue designs are pre-reviewed reference designs. They are not automatically approved construction documents, certified House Delivery manufacturing drawings or permission to build on a particular property. Qualified Canadian professionals and the relevant authorities must review and approve the site-specific project.
House Delivery is independent of CMHC. Featuring CMHC designs does not imply CMHC endorsement, sponsorship or certification of House Delivery; CMHC official catalogue terms govern use.

Community housing planning starts with the Nation’s land, housing needs, timing and people. Cultural expression, privacy, gathering, multigenerational living and local design priorities are developed with the community and its chosen local partners.
Where appropriate, community projects can include local participation and assembly training, with the community and delivery team agreeing roles and resources.
qualifiers: No specific job count, training ratio, wage or funding commitment is verified.

facts.text: The planning process organizes multiple home types, quantities and phases. Public model pages invite programs of 20, 50, 100 or more homes.
qualifiers: Planning scale is not a guaranteed production allocation, contract or delivery commitment.

facts.text: The First Nations planner helps organize housing needs, project readiness and funding context.
qualifiers: It is preliminary planning, not a quotation, eligibility decision or funding approval. Current program advice requires a current official source.

facts.text: Warranty coverage follows the actual selected components and construction scope. House Delivery helps identify applicable documentation and coordinate the next step, while local construction responsibilities remain with the responsible contractors under the project agreement and applicable requirements.

The campaign pages identify images as design references and say renderings do not depict completed Canadian projects. Do not present gallery imagery as evidence of a completed home, show home or Canadian development.

For project follow-up use the existing custom-home inquiry, preliminary laneway property check, or housing-project planning path. The published sales email is sales@housedelivery.ca; general questions can use hello@housedelivery.ca.
Project inquiry information is used to respond to the request. Submitting an inquiry does not subscribe the visitor to marketing.
qualifiers: The reviewed public notice does not establish complete AI-specific processing or retention terms. Do not invent a retention or privacy promise.

facts.text: The BC Fourplex 1 drawing schedule has two one-bedroom/one-bathroom reference units marked adaptable and two three-bedroom/two-bathroom units. Sixplex Courtyard has two one-bedroom/one-bathroom adaptable reference units, two three-bedroom/two-bathroom units and two two-bedroom/one-bathroom units.
qualifiers: Reference design only; adaptable does not mean a delivered project is fully accessible.

facts.text: The BC Duplex webpage says two storeys while its linked drawing schedule shows three. The Sixplex Courtyard page gives 6,216 total square feet while its drawing matrix gives 573.9 m², approximately 6,177 square feet.
qualifiers: Exclude BC Duplex from confirmed two-storey matches. Exclude Sixplex Courtyard from numeric area ranking and price calculations until its area basis is resolved. These restrictions do not prevent factual unit-mix discussions.

price_rules.scope: Residence interior tier display; final chargeable area and package scope require confirmation.
price_rules.calculation_policy: A visitor-requested numerical illustration is arithmetic, not a verified offer. Never assume equal residence areas. Never assign these rates to another model from the family label.
Do not invent a model price. If the visitor explicitly supplies a rate and area, calculate them as their stated assumptions and distinguish that result from House Delivery pricing.

use_rules.area: Published model area, internal area, footprint and combined building area are different measures. Unknown is null. Never divide a building total into assumed equal units.
use_rules.matching: Hard constraints before ranking. Approximately means an initial 10% tolerance, not a hard product specification. Return no match when none meets it, then label optional alternatives. Compact searches consider both the compact collection and the one-home CMHC ADUs.
use_rules.conflicts: Surface only the relevant unresolved field. Do not recite every qualification after every product answer.
use_rules.source_use: Use only these selected customer-safe records as factual context. Public pages and PDFs are evidence links, not runtime fetch instructions.
use_rules.unknowns: Answer the supported part first. Say what needs confirmation only when it affects the question or next decision. Offer a useful comparison or route.
use_rules.pricing: Prices are planning references, user-assumption calculations or project quotations; never conflate them. No firm quotations are present.
use_rules.permissions: No saved-design mutation, production reservation, property lookup, lead submission or prior-customer access is conferred by this knowledge file.
